result.markdown: --- title: "06 · The t-test as a linear model" subtitle: "Week 2" --- ::: {.guiding-q} Isn't a t-test something else? ::: ## In this session - The independent-samples *t*-test is a regression with one binary predictor - The one-sample and the paired *t*-test are intercept-only models - Welch's *t*-test and what it changes (unequal variances) - Why this matters: one framework instead of a decision tree of tests ::: {.key-terms} **Key terms:** [*p*-value](../../glossary.qmd#p-value), [Degrees of freedom](../../glossary.qmd#df) ::: ## Learning goals After this session you can - reproduce a *t*-test with `lm()` and show that the results are identical, - explain what the intercept and the slope correspond to in a *t*-test, - run a paired *t*-test as a model of differences. ## Simulate first ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(6) group <- factor(rep(c("young", "old"), each = 25), levels = c("young", "old")) y <- rnorm(50, ifelse(group == "old", 12, 10), 3) t.test(y ~ group, var.equal = TRUE)$statistic # classic t-test ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> t #> -1.736361 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} summary(lm(y ~ group))$coefficients # same t (sign flipped), same p ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) #> (Intercept) 10.480585 0.6348610 16.508472 2.003183e-21 #> groupold 1.558956 0.8978291 1.736361 8.891506e-02 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.box} **Paired *t*-test** = intercept-only model of the differences: `lm(after - before ~ 1)`. ::: ## Materials ::: {.materials} - Slides coming soon - R script coming soon - Exercises coming soon ::: ## Reading - Lindeløv, J. K. (2019). *Common statistical tests are linear models (or: how to teach stats).*
